resources.instruction: Before choosing needs_info to ask a person: (1) read the README, the relevant documents and the nearby code, because anything you can find in the repository you must not ask; ask only when the repository has contradictory evidence, lacks context, needs a business judgement, or the work is hard to undo. (2) In needs-info.md write the analysis first: what you looked for and why you could not decide. (3) Give 2 to 4 concrete options, each able to stand on its own (understandable when read alone), with its impact; mark the option you recommend and why. The reviewer sees only what you write: do not ask about analysis they have not read.

Group the questions so the reviewer can answer them in one pass: Scope (what to do, what not to do, minimal or complete version); Assumptions (what you take as true and what breaks if it is not); Trade-offs (A or B); Risks (dependencies, what could break); Architecture (organisation, data, API). Write each question in full, with its options and why this decision affects the implementation. A good question exposes a hidden decision; it does not merely confirm the obvious.
